caption: What if the real top of the world isn't Everest? Everest stands 8,849 metres above sea level, the highest point on Earth. But Earth isn't a perfect ball: its spin makes it bulge at the equator, so the equator sits about 21 km farther from Earth's centre than the poles. Chimborazo in Ecuador is only 6,263 metres tall, but it sits just one degree south of the equator, right on that bulge. Its peak is about 6,384 km from Earth's centre, roughly 2 km farther out than the top of Everest, which makes it the point on Earth's surface farthest from the centre. Bonus: gravity is a little weaker at the equator, so you'd weigh about 0.5% less there than at the poles. The plot twist: measured from its base on the sea floor, Hawaii's Mauna Kea is about 10,200 metres tall, taller than Everest. So which one is the REAL top of the world for YOU? 👇
